sections.h2: Why the county line matters in Draper
sections.html:
Draper sits on the Wasatch Front about 20 miles south of Salt Lake City, and the city spans two counties: Salt Lake and Utah. It covers roughly 30 square miles at 4,751 feet, at the Point of the Mountain between the Salt Lake and Utah valleys.

For a seller, the county line decides which assessor values the house, which treasurer sends the bill and which recorder files the deed. School districts differ too: Canyons on the Salt Lake County side and Alpine on the Utah County side. Check the parcel number on your tax notice before you plan anything, because two neighbors a few blocks apart can deal with different offices, calendars and school boundaries.

Draper had 51,017 residents in 2020, up from 7,257 in 1990. Many neighborhoods were built in that window, so houses range from old farm lots to subdivisions less than a generation old. The median home value is $784,800, median gross rent is $1,894, and 68.6% of homes are owner-occupied. That leaves roughly 31% rented, so if you are selling a rental, the tenant situation matters as much as the building.

Foothill homes can be affected. In December 2025 the city council adopted Ordinance 1695, creating a Wildland Urban Interface Area in the city code. The public notice does not map the boundaries or spell out the rules, so ask the city for the full ordinance if your lot backs onto open hillside.

A separate state program adds another layer. Utah House Bill 48 of 2025 led the state forestry division to publish a wildfire risk map scoring each building from 1 to 8. A building that scores 7 or higher and sits within 250 meters of at least two other buildings falls inside the high-risk boundary, and its owner may owe the state an annual fee once the program starts, which the state expected later in 2026.

  • Look up the address at wildfirerisk.utah.gov before you list or accept an offer.
  • Keep a printout of the score for the buyer or title company.
  • Ask the Draper City planning office whether your lot falls inside the new city interface area.

Running a short-term rental in Draper takes two approvals: a business license and a short-term rental permit. A stay is short term when it is under 30 consecutive days, the minimum stay is two nights, and the permit must be renewed every year. Each day of unpermitted operation is its own violation.

Accessory dwelling units have separate limits.

  • A detached ADU needs a residential lot of at least 12,000 square feet.
  • An internal ADU generally needs a residential lot over 6,000 square feet on a qualifying street, and the city has mapped areas where internal units are banned.
  • The owner must live in the main dwelling for both types.
  • ADU rentals must run at least 30 consecutive days, and each needs one extra on-site parking space.

A basement apartment built without a permit is a common snag. Owners who did not apply by February 1, 2022 face immediate enforcement, so a buyer who needs financing may hesitate. Draper's planning office answers questions at (801) 576-6399.

Whichever county bills you, Utah gives a primary residence a 45% exemption, so only 55% of market value is taxed. Rental homes can qualify as primary residences under state rules, and vacation homes cannot.

Parcel inTax noticesDue datePenalty on December 1
Salt Lake CountyValuation notices July 22, tax notices by November 1November 30Greater of 2.5% or $10 per parcel
Utah CountyThird week of OctoberNovember 30Greater of 1% or $10

On the Salt Lake County side, the Board of Equalization takes valuation appeals from August 1 to September 15. If your house is on the market when the notice arrives, tell the title officer so the current-year bill is handled correctly at closing.

A cash sale follows the same steps as any Utah sale, minus the lender.

  1. Tell us about the house, including any tenants, liens or repairs.
  2. We look at the property and the recent sales around it.
  3. You decide whether to accept the offer or walk away.
  4. A title company runs the title search and prepares the closing paperwork.
  5. The deed is recorded with the county recorder where the parcel sits.

Recording is cheap. Salt Lake County charges a flat $40 recording fee, and Utah County lists the same $40 standard fee per document. Salt Lake County also wants a notary acknowledgment, the grantee's address and the tax serial number on the deed. You choose the closing date with the title company.

Start with the parcel number and the most recent tax notice, since both tell you which county's offices apply. Then collect any ADU permit or application receipt, the short-term rental permit and its renewal date, a printout of the state wildfire score, and your loan payoff details. If tenants live there, add the lease.

Handing the title officer this folder at the start avoids the back-and-forth that slows many Draper closings. It also lets the buyer see exactly what the house is and is not permitted to do before the contract is signed.

A few issues come up again and again.

  • A hillside lot with a high state wildfire score.
  • An older basement unit with no ADU permit.
  • A short-term rental permit that lapsed after its annual renewal.
  • A tenant in place on a rental.
  • Confusion over whether the parcel is billed by Salt Lake County or Utah County.

Each of these can be solved, but each adds steps to a traditional listing. A direct sale lets you sell the house as it stands and deal with the paperwork at the title company.

Draper is part of the Silicon Slopes tech corridor, and the city reports more than 1,000 businesses. Interstate 15 runs through town, the TRAX Blue Line stops at Draper Town Center and Kimballs Lane, and a FrontRunner station is also in the city. Salt Lake International Airport and Provo Municipal Airport are each about 30 minutes away by car. Buyers who work in tech or commute by rail often ask how close a house is to those stations.

faqs.q: Is Draper in Salt Lake County or Utah County?
faqs.a: Both. The county for your tax bill and deed depends on the parcel, so check the parcel number on your tax notice.

faqs.q: When are Draper property taxes due?
faqs.a: November 30 in either county. If the date falls on a weekend or holiday it moves to the next business day.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to rent my Draper house short term?
faqs.a: Yes, both a business license and a short-term rental permit, and the permit must be renewed each year. Each day without them counts as a separate violation.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Draper house that has an unpermitted basement apartment?
faqs.a: Yes, but expect questions. Draper requires an ADU permit before an accessory unit is rented, and the owner must live in the main dwelling. A cash buyer can take the house as it is, while a financed buyer may ask you to resolve the permit first.

faqs.q: How do I check wildfire risk for a Draper address?
faqs.a: Search the address at wildfirerisk.utah.gov. It shows a score from 1 to 8, and buildings scoring 7 or higher near other buildings are treated as high risk.
